population: The 201 Bug tickets docs/papers/harbour/reliability-baseline-defects.json (LIN-3149) judged escaped or escaped-test, LIN-26 to LIN-3122, both repos.
method: Each defect read from its one-line reason, repo, introducing ticket and finder in that file, by one in-session subagent against the rubric below, fixed before reading; at most two rules per defect. Not second-read.

rubric.regression-history: The fault re-breaks behaviour a previous commit had fixed, or re-applies something reverted.
rubric.class-check: The fault is a sibling instance of a class another change fixed/handled (same bug in a second place, a missed caller/route/variant).
rubric.mutation-check: Tests passed while the claimed code path was not wired in / the code did not take effect; a vacuous or non-load-bearing test.
rubric.test-adequacy: The fault is cross-module or user-facing and would need an e2e/integration test that was absent.
rubric.direct-verification: Visible only by looking at the running page/UI or real behaviour (visual/layout/rendering), not by tests.
rubric.requirements: The shipped change did not meet its own ticket's stated requirement/acceptance criteria.
rubric.quality-checklist: Security/credential flaw, error handling, performance regression.
rubric.inside-outside: The fault was a known inside-scope item that was discharged by filing instead of doing it (with ledger-discharge).
rubric.ledger-discharge: The fault was a known inside-scope item that was discharged by filing instead of doing it (with inside-outside).
rubric.trivial-edit-bound: A close-out authored/merged content review never saw, and that content was faulty.
rubric.risk-lanes: A claim that could only be proven in production, accepted without a firing monitor, that then failed.
rubric.archive-prune: A fault in/caused by the description prune or archive step.
rubric.follow-up-filing: Follow-ups filed untriaged/with wrong priority causing the fault to sit.
rubric.ci-green-exact-commit: Merged on red CI or on a commit other than the reviewed one.
rubric.none: No rule's class fits (e.g. provider/API behaviour change, environment, novel design gap).
